title: Sticky cache: oddities and hypotheses — weekly digest
content:
Purpose: quick weekly digest from the sticky-cache troubleshooting sessions (May 3–9, 2028). Goal is to capture concrete observations, non-obvious hypotheses, short experiments run, and a prioritized set of follow-ups with clear owners. This is a working note — rough, intentionally terse.

Attendees: Olivia (owner), Riya, Marcus, Diego, Priya; ad-hoc from SRE: Anil; product-soundoff: Lina.

Summary (tl;dr):
- We continue to see persistent "sticky" KV entries for a small fraction (~0.6%) of user sessions causing elevated p95/p99 token latencies on m-class backends.
- Sticky pattern appears correlated with long prefix re-use (chat sessions > 2k tokens) combined with async prefill race conditions when kernel v3.4.2 hit a backpressure window.
- Short experiments suggest a fix-space: (A) enforce a fast-path TTL on cached KV when reattach_count > 1; (B) tighten prefill acknowledgement ordering in the coalescer; (C) a conservative eviction boost for long-tail sessions.

Concrete observations and evidence:
1) Metric snippet from 2028-05-06 00:00–23:59 (prod-cluster-a):
   - overall cache hit rate: 87.3%
   - for sessions with >1500 tokens: hit rate 95.9% but those sessions make up 0.9% of calls and 6.8% of tail latency noise
   - p95 token-latency spike correlated with sharp drop in async-prefill-acks for ~30-minute window (00:42–01:15)
2) Traces (attached in linked_artifacts PR and Confluence): repeated order of events for affected requests: reattach -> prefill start -> prefill enqueue -> prefill delayed by coalescer -> request proceeds with stale KV -> deopt pathway triggers synchronous prefill -> long-tail serialization stalls
3) Heap snapshots from kernel worker show lingering KV entries with reference-count=0 but pinned_in_cache=true for ~8–12 minutes. These appear to be the "sticky" entries.
4) Kernel variant note: v3.4.1 does not show the same long-tail as v3.4.2 in a 6-hour A/B run (control vs candidate). v3.4.2 introduced a micro-optimization for coalescer queue head skipping; hypothesis is the fast-path changed ordering during backpressure.

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1 (high priority): coalescer head-skip optimization in v3.4.2 can cause prefill acks to be reordered under parity pressure; stale KV can be marked pinned due to a race between eviction and reattach logic.
H2 (medium): long prefix sessions accidentally mark KV entries as "session-sticky" via a combination of reattach_count increments and the new TTL-preservation logic added for resumable sessions. Edge-case triggers when prefill is queued but not acknowledged.
H3 (low): hardware-induced thread scheduling jitter on hot workers is exacerbating the above races during 30s–120s load bursts.

Experiments run (short):
- EXP-2028-05-05-A: force-coalescer-fifo toggle (candidate off) in canary cluster. Result: tail p99 dropped 9% during the observed window; sticky count decreased but not eliminated. (JIRA-RT-8812)
- EXP-2028-05-06-B: TTL-slab trial — add a short TTL bump (1m) for KV entries created during reattach. Result: immediate decrease in pinned_in_cache duration from median 8m -> 56s, but small throughput hit (~1.6%).
- EXP-2028-05-08-C: instrumentation-only run to emit per-request prefill state machine traces (no behavior change). Outcome: allowed us to pinpoint reattach ordering in 74% of reproduced traces.

Decisions from sync (May 8):
- Roll forward: do NOT roll back v3.4.2 across all clusters. The cost/benefit still favors v3.4.2 performance for common workloads.
- Short-term mitigation: implement a targeted per-session TTL sweep for reattached KV entries (prototype in PR linked). This is low-risk and reversible. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 48 hours for canary.
- Mid-term: revert head-skip optimization and replace with ordering-safe coalescer logic if short-term mitigations fail. Owner: Riya. ETA: 2 weeks.

Action items (concrete):
- M1: Marcus -> push canary of TTL-sweep change (PR 4127) to prod-canary cluster, monitor p95/p99 and pinned_in_cache metric. Tag: canary-ttl-0508. Due: 2028-05-11.
- M2: Diego -> add a telemetry counter that increments when prefill-ack order != pref entry creation order. Emit to metrics prefix runtime.prefill.order_mismatch. Due: 2028-05-10.
- M3: Riya -> write revertable patch for head-skip -> ordering-safe coalescer; prepare A/B harness. JIRA: RT-8841. Due: 2028-05-22.
- M4: Priya -> coordinate customer-impact list with CS for sessions >10k tokens, prepare comms if mitigation requires rolling change. Due: 2028-05-13.
- M5: Olivia -> run long-tail replay harness (reproducer) with 10x amplification and capture full traces. Due: 2028-05-12.

Notes on risk and rollback strategy:
- The TTL-sweep change is a best-effort mitigation. It does not change eviction ordering globally, only shortens the lifetime of KV entries created during a reattach window. If we see regressions in throughput >3%, we will revert and try the ordering-safe coalescer quicker.
- Full revert of v3.4.2 is an option but expensive; we will only consider it if early mitigations fail to reduce p99 by >=15% during next 72-hour window.

Open questions (to resolve next sync):
- Q1: What is the minimum TTL we can enforce without increasing CPU spend significantly? (Diego)
- Q2: How often do affected sessions correlate with specific models (decoder-only vs chat transformer)? Could model-specific KV layout be a contributing factor? (Priya)
- Q3: If we revert head-skip, what micro-benchmarks do we need to run to be confident we won't regress throughput for the 50k qps baseline? (Riya)

Ancillary findings and low-priority notes:
- Observed odd serialization where a client library reattach path calls reattach twice in <200ms causing our state machine to increment reattach_count unexpectedly. Filing CL in client-kit (linked) to add a de-dupe guard.
- SRE noticed correlated disk-iowait in one host during the window; likely unrelated but flagged.

Meeting cadence: keep this group weekly for two cycles, then reduce cadence to ad-hoc if mitigations prove stable. Next sync: 2028-05-15 09:30 PT (standup room + zoom).

Appendix: quick reproduction steps for local dev harness (for folks who will pick up the ticket):
1) checkout branch exp/ttl-sweep-4127
2) run harness: scripts/run_replayer --sessions 1000 --long-tail 0.8 --amplify 10 --duration 600
3) watch metrics: local.promtail: runtime.prefill.order_mismatch, runtime.kv.pinned_in_cache_seconds
4) If pinned_in_cache_seconds median >120s, collect worker heap and upload to Confluence-1234.

If you have additions, paste into this doc or slack thread #serving-runtime and I will fold into the next digest.

-- Olivia
